summary: Palau admits visitors of nearly every nationality with a free 30-day entry permit issued on arrival; citizens of the Schengen states are visa-free for 90 days in any 180 and Russians for 30 days, while nationals of Bangladesh and Myanmar must apply before travelling. US, Micronesian and Marshallese citizens enter freely under the Compact of Free Association. Everyone pays the USD 100 Pristine Paradise Environmental Fee and signs the Palau Pledge stamped into their passport.

payments.text: The Government of Canada says major credit cards are accepted at most hotels and tourist facilities. The UK FCDO says doctors and medical centres often expect immediate cash payment, and warns of an increase in credit card fraud.

safety.text: Crime levels are low — theft of unattended items is more likely than confrontational crime — but credit card fraud, including skimming, has increased. In the water, take local advice before swimming or diving from high rocks: there are over 60 vertical drop-offs, some for experienced divers only, so check a dive operator's credentials and that safety equipment, particularly oxygen, is on the boat.

tips.text: The UK FCDO says you must sign the Palau Pledge, which is stamped in your passport on arrival. Submit the Palau Entry Form online in the 72 hours before you depart; it generates a QR code to show at check-in and on arrival.

The USD 100 Pristine Paradise Environmental Fee is included in the price of your air ticket into Palau — international airlines are required to add it. If you are exempt (for example a transit passenger or crew) and were charged, claim the cash refund on arrival with your itinerary.

Visiting the Rock Islands needs a Koror State use permit on top of your tour price: USD 50 for the Rock Islands, or USD 100 for the Jellyfish Lake permit, which covers the lake as well. Permits are valid for 10 days and are required from age 6, according to the Koror State Government's fact sheet.

It is illegal to bring or use reef-toxic sunscreen in Palau, and the UK FCDO says customs will confiscate it from your baggage. Pack sunscreen whose active ingredient is zinc oxide or titanium dioxide.

The UK FCDO says Palau’s only hyperbaric chamber is at Belau National Hospital in Koror and that diving school standards are not always as high as in the UK. Check a dive operator’s credentials, make sure oxygen is carried on the boat, and ask how divers would be transferred to the chamber.

faq.question: Do I need a visa for Palau?
faq.answer: For a normal holiday, no. Visitors of nearly every nationality are issued a free entry permit on arrival valid for 30 days, provided they hold a passport valid six months, an onward ticket and somewhere to stay. US, Micronesian and Marshallese citizens enter freely under the Compact of Free Association. Citizens of the Schengen states need no visa for up to 90 days in any 180-day period, and nationals of Bangladesh and Myanmar must apply for a visa before they travel.

faq.question: What is the Palau Pledge?
faq.answer: It is an eco-pledge stamped into every visitor’s passport on arrival. The UK FCDO says you must sign it as part of border control.

faq.question: How much is Palau's environmental fee?
faq.answer: The Pristine Paradise Environmental Fee is USD 100 for every visitor coming to Palau. International airlines are required to include it in the price of tickets into Palau, so you pay it when you book. Palauan passport holders and their spouses, crew, accredited diplomats and transit passengers are exempt and can claim a cash refund on arrival.

faq.question: Can I stay in Palau longer than 30 days?
faq.answer: Yes. The Division of Immigration in Koror can extend the tourist visa for up to two further 30-day periods, for a USD 50 renewal fee each time. Apply at least seven days before your current visa expires.

faq.question: Is sunscreen really banned in Palau?
faq.answer: Reef-toxic sunscreen is. The UK FCDO says it is illegal to bring it into Palau or use it there, that customs will confiscate it, and that there are penalties for selling it. Permitted sunscreens generally use zinc oxide or titanium dioxide as the active ingredient.
